verdict.rationale: Cloudflare's docs claim Workers run with 'No cold starts', which implies near-instant boot. The scale claim ('scaling to tens of millions of instances', 'run millions of them') is made for Agents SDK instances built on Durable Objects on the Workers platform, not explicitly for plain Worker autoscaling under load. Missing for 10: explicit sub-second boot-time figures, documented autoscaling behavior for Workers under traffic spikes, and independent or hands-on corroboration of either boot latency or scale.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can deploy instances that boot in under a second and scale to tens of thousands under load

citations.quote: No servers to manage. No cold starts or region complexity.
Deploy once and Cloudflare runs your agents across its global network, scaling to tens of millions of instances.
Agents hibernate when idle and wake on demand. You can run millions of them
